slice: Every object in the treehouse drawn as pixel art in place of its plain box, in Ed's mismatched style: cottage pieces sprouting leaves, the odd gothic one, and modern clutter (#1017)
built: `art/furniture.js`: each of the house's 25 objects as a 3D model, built from its footprint in `config/house.json` and never from where it stands, so the house's layout can move it. It includes a gothic canopy bed with a hoodie and a glowing phone on it, a clothes rail strung with fairy lights, a bulb-lit vanity, the crystal ball on its clawed brass stand, curtains that are shut while she wakes, a cauldron with the last of a brew glowing in it, a record shelf with a lava lamp, a pegboard with a neon bolt, a cabinet of skulls, a telescope and the locked bedrooms' doors
A palette for each room, and lights of every kind: candles, bulbs, fairy lights, neon, screens and magic. Each piece lights what's near it, as the creator's room does

Ed's answers on the mock: the pieces twice their real size, the bed's canopy over its head half, the rooms dim with the glows carrying them, and fewer, chunkier things of clutter that read at a glance

`render/houseFurniture.ts` turns each piece to face its room's middle and bakes it, the nearest first, a piece a frame. `render/houseRooms.ts` draws them between each room's floor and its near rail. `tools/house/organic.mjs` gives each piece its size and puts its back to the rim of Golf's round rooms
`tools/house/furniture-sheet.mjs` draws them all as a contact sheet without a browser; `tools/house/furniture-shots.cjs` shoots each room in the game
learned: Detail that reads on a contact sheet can turn to noise in the game, where the lighting and the pixel style flatten it. Fewer, bigger things read better. Asking Ed four multiple-choice questions on a mock of four pieces settled the style before the other 21 were drawn
A piece facing any angle beats a mirrored one: mirroring flips the light with it, and a round room's arc wants every angle
